histamine-induced, NO-mediated relaxation in human omentum resistance arteries is attenuated in pre-eclamspic pregnancy.
histamine-induced endothelium-dependent relaxation in resistance arteries is reduced in pre-eclamptics and that this may be explained, at least in pa, by a reduced action of cGMP in smooth muscle.

the histamine induced, endothelium- derived NO-mediated relaxation (via H(1)- receptors) is down-regulat-ed in resistance arteries in preeclampsia and that this is due to an attenuation of cGMP action in smooth muscle cells.

a better understanding of the mechanisms underlying the pathophysiological changes in the vasculature in pregnancy and the development of new therapeutic strategies for pre-eclampsic patients.

the characteristic changes in the vascular responses of the resistance arteries seen in pregnancy-induced hypertension (pre-eclampsia), a common complication of pregnancy, which is associated with a high risk of perinatal mortality.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the histamine induced, endothelium derived, nitric oxide mediated relaxation (mediated through H1-receptors) is down regulated in resistance arteries in Pre-Eclampsia.

the histamine receptor-mediated endothelium-dependent relaxation in human omenta resistance arteries is attenuated in pre-eclamptics and that this is due to an attenuation of cyclic GMP formation in smooth muscle cells.
the endothelial function in resistance arteries in women with pre-eclampsis is altered in such a way that it is less able to respond to histamine-induced stimulation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the NO-cGMP pathway is attenuated in resistance vessels in pre-eclamspia and that this contributes to the hypertension of the disorder.
histamine-induced, NO-mediated relaxation is attenuated in resistance arteries in preeclampsia and this attenuation may be due to an attenuation of cGMP-mediated smooth muscle cell relaxation.

the endothelium-derived relaxing factor (EDRF)/endothelium-dependent hyperpolarizing factor (EDHF) system is altered in resistance arteries in pregnancy-induced hypertension (PIH) and that these changes are more pronounced in the severe form of PIH, pre-eclampsic.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the NO-mediated relaxation induced by histamines is attenuated in pre-eclamtic patients.
histamine-induced relaxation of resistance arteries is attenuated in pre-eclamptics, which may be due to the attenuation of the action on cyclic GMP in the smooth muscle.
the histamine receptor H(1)-mediated NO-mediated vasorelaxation is down-regulated, which is due at least in part to an attenuation of cyclic GMP action in smooth muscle cells in pre-eclamptics.
